::: {.callout-note}
## Goals

1. Read in every participant's data file at once
2. Keep only the rating trials
3. Find the average rating for each image, and plot it
:::

DataPipe saves **one CSV file per participant**. This document reads all of
them, stacks them into one table, and summarizes the ratings.

## (1) Load packages

Run this once, by hand, if you have never installed these.

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "here"))
```

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

## (2) Read in all the data files

The files in `data/example/` came from three practice runs of the experiment.
Once you have real data, download the files from your DataPipe storage
(e.g., your Google Drive folder) into `data/raw/`, and change `"example"` to
`"raw"` below.

```{r}
data_folder <- here("data", "example")

# Make a list of every .csv file in that folder
files <- list.files(data_folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
files
```

`read_csv()` can read a whole list of files and stack them into one table.

```{r}
all_data <- read_csv(files, show_col_types = FALSE)

glimpse(all_data)
```

Each participant contributes several rows: one for each screen they saw
(welcome, instructions, each image, goodbye).

## (3) Keep only the rating trials

We gave every rating screen `task = "rating"` in `index.html`, so we can
filter on it. We also shorten the image name from
`stimuli/red_circle.png` to `red_circle`.

```{r}
ratings <- all_data |>
  filter(task == "rating") |>
  mutate(image = str_remove(basename(stimulus), "\\.png$")) |>
  select(participant_id, image, rating, rt)

ratings
```

Quick checks: how many participants, and did everyone rate every image?

```{r}
ratings |>
  count(participant_id)
```

## (4) Average rating per image

```{r}
image_means <- ratings |>
  group_by(image) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rating = mean(rating),
    n = n()
  )

image_means
```

```{r}
ggplot(ratings, aes(x = image, y = rating)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = image_means, aes(y = mean_rating), color = "red", size = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7) +
  labs(
    x = "Image",
    y = "Rating (1 = not at all, 7 = very much)",
    title = "Black dots = individual ratings; red dots = averages"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The example data are random clicks, so do not read anything into the pattern.
